newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Commodities fund looks at five-year action plan.
newsitem.headline: Commodities fund looks at five-year action plan.

text.p: The governing council of the Common Fund for Commodities met in the Moroccan city of Marrakesh on Monday to follow up experts' recommendations on its future activities.
A report from the Fund's executive board asked the governors to seek a five-year action plan based on "workable suggestions made by the experts".

The report, a copy of which was seen by Reuters, said some proposals by three experts on future direction were felt to be "too wide-ranging and...inappropriate or difficult to implement for the Common Fund which should build on current activities."

The fund's aims are to help finance international buffer stocks and support commodity development projects. The report said it was important to remember that "ultimate beneficiaries are poorer sections of the population, namely those in the agricultural sector...."
A summary of operations of the fund's Second Account -- for development projects -- said by the end of 1996 it had backed 49 projects covering 20 commodities with a total cost of $118.1 million.
The commodities included bananas, citrus, cocoa, coconut, coffee, cotton, groundnuts, oil palm, olive oil, rice, rubber, sisal, sugar, tea, timber and zinc.
"The fund provided total financing in the equivalent of $52.6 million of which the equivalent of $2.57 million was provided as loan," the report said.
Among future projects approved by the directors and being submitted to the governing council were:

- development of gourmet coffee potential, creation of pilot demonstration plants and training to improve olive oil quality, and "sustainable productivity improvement for rice in inland valleys in West Africa".
According to the report, three projects were completed during 1996. One in rubber and one in jute successfully developed new processes to produce better products.
The summary of Second Account resources said total resources at end-1996 were projected at SDR77.71 million, of which SDR36.26 million had been committed.
Switzerland is to withdraw from the fund on December 31.
